ref_text.narrator: Twelve hundred years ago, they did not build a temple. They carved one, out of a living mountain.

voices.narrator_epic: male, middle-aged, very low pitch, british accent

jobs.text: Inside Tirumala temple, there is a secret kitchen.
Every single day, it makes around three lakh laddus.
By hand. Without stopping. Watch how.
This is Tirumala, in Andhra Pradesh. The temple sits on the seventh of seven hills.
Inside is the Laddu Potu, the temple kitchen.
About six hundred and twenty cooks work here.
They have made this laddu since seventeen fifteen. Over three hundred years.
First, the ingredients. Every single day.
Ten tonnes of gram flour. Ten tonnes of sugar.
Seven hundred kilos of cashews. Five hundred and forty kilos of raisins. One hundred and fifty kilos of cardamom.
Step one: batter drops into hot ghee, and becomes boondi.
Step two: the boondi is mixed with sugar syrup, cashews, raisins and cardamom.
Step three: every laddu is rolled by hand.
Conveyor belts carry raw materials in, and laddus out.
Since two thousand and nine, the name Tirupati laddu is protected by a G I tag.
And on big festival days, this kitchen can make up to eight lakh laddus in one day.
Follow for more secrets like this.
